title: Starter UX + Economics: Phrases and Plays
content:
Purpose:
A compact, engineer-facing playbook of messaging, short quickstart sequences, and small pricing experiments intended for the Hosted API product page, SDK quickstarts, and the first two onboarding emails. Focus: make the first call feel trivial, align pricing language to developer decision moments, and provide rebuttals for cost/latency objections.

Top-line positioning hypothesis (single sentence):
For engineers who need predictable performance and an easy path to production, Redwood’s Hosted API provides production-grade inference primitives with immediate SDK ergonomics, transparent unit economics, and hands-off scaling so teams ship fast without sacrificing latency or cost controls.

Key developer-first value props (short):
- Instant endpoint: make a complete model call in < 2 minutes with an SDK sample and one environment variable.
- Predictable performance: benchmarks and a small, clear SLA for per-route p50/p95 latency visible in the Console.
- Cost clarity: per-token math shown with an example snippet for a 200-token chat and an embedding use case.
- Safe defaults for production: rate-limits, canary rollouts, automatic fallback to cheaper variants.

Quickstart angles (two complementary flows):
- 2-minute trial (zero friction):
  1) Create account, hit "Get API Key"; copy key.
  2) npm i @redwood/infer && run: node ./examples/quick-chat.js
  3) See streaming response in console; modify prompt and call again.
  Quick messaging line: "From zero to a chat in under two minutes — no infra, no config."

- 30-minute stub-to-prod (engineer to PM to demo):
  1) Starter template repo (chat + embeddings + simple rerank) — one branch ready to deploy to Vercel/EC2.
  2) Add API key and a single env var for MODEL override to toggle cheaper/fast models.
  3) Toggle canary: 10% users to cheaper quantized model, 90% to default.
  Measurement hook: shipping route-level p95 and cost-per-1000-requests to a dashboard.
  Quick messaging line: "Prototype today, ship a low-risk canary tomorrow."

Pricing-language drafts (microcopy + examples):
- Headline snippet for pricing page: "Simple per-request pricing + optional reserved capacity. Pay for what you use, not for guesswork."
- Microcopy under SKU: "Text generation: $X per 1K input tokens, $Y per 1K output tokens. Embeddings: $Z per 1K vectors." (A/B test ranges: X=$0.012–$0.018, Y=$0.016–$0.022, Z=$0.004–$0.007)
- Developer-facing example (show math):
  "Example: a 200-input/300-output token chat costs ~$0.009 (at $0.015/1K input + $0.02/1K output)."
- Free credit framing: "$100 in free credits for new signups, valid for 60 days. Enough for ~5k chat requests at typical prompt sizes."
- Starter tier trial: "Starter seats: $200/mo includes 100k tokens + basic SLA and priority support during onboarding."
- Pricing safety rails copy: "Set hard token budgets per-key, or enable automatic fallback to cached responses when budgets hit thresholds."

Small pricing experiments to run (4 wks each):
- Experiment A: $100 vs $200 free-credit gift for signups — measure activation (1st API call), retention (3 calls/week) and billing conversion.
- Experiment B: Show explicit cost math on quickstart vs hide math behind a "Pricing" link — measure conversion to adding API key and time-to-first-call.
- Experiment C: Offer pre-configured "Starter Seat" (monthly) vs pure usage billing — measure percent of teams that pick Starter Seat within 30 days.

Competitive notes (concise):
- Big cloud LLM endpoints (GCP/AWS equivalents): advantage = scale and legacy trust; disadvantage = opaque performance tradeoffs, multi-step config for multi-model routing. Message: emphasize Redwood’s predictable per-route latency, transparent perf profiles, and one SDK to switch between hosted/dedicated/private.
- API-first LLM SaaS (simplicity-focused rivals): advantage = very low friction; disadvantage = limited enterprise controls and unpredictable cost under load. Message: keep friction low but lead with unit economics and safety-rails.
- Self-hosted runtimes / OSS stacks: advantage = control and potentially lower cost; disadvantage = ops overhead. Message: Redwood reduces ops burden with autoscaling + cost-aware batching while letting customers export to Dedicated/Private when they want control.

Objection handling (short snippets):
- "Too expensive": "We show exact per-request math in the SDK examples. Try the free credits to validate cost on your prompts before committing."
- "Latency varies": "Routes have measured p50/p95 published in the Console and fallbacks that keep your app responding while higher-tier capacity spins up."
- "We need data isolation": "Private and Dedicated options let you pin to customer-specific pools and integrate with your KMS — same API surface as Hosted."

Suggested microcopy for SDK docs (short lines):
- Onboarding banner: "Start your first inference in <2 minutes — copy the key and run the sample."
- Billing CTA near quickstart: "Estimate cost for your prompt" (opens inline calculator prefilled with the sample).

Measurement plan (what success looks like in 90 days):
- Time-to-first-call median <= 3m for new accounts.
- % users who make 3+ calls in first week >= 25% (activation).
- Conversion to paid usage within 60 days >= 6% for accounts that used free credits.
- A/B metric: showing cost math on quickstart improves activation by +12–18%.

Open questions & next steps:
- Decide exact free-credit amount (A/B test two sizes).
- Implement inline cost calculator on quickstart page (engineering ticket).
- Prepare a short canary email sequence for teams after first API call (hand-off to growth).

Appendix: sample email subject lines (for onboarding sequence):
- "Your Redwood API key is ready — try a quick demo in 2 minutes"
- "How to ship a demo: sample app + cost estimate"
- "Ready to scale? Tips to control token costs and route performance"

This doc is intended to seed copy for the public quickstart page, a 2-email onboarding drip for new signups, and the internal GTM experiments backlog. Please review and flag any legal/product constraints around free credits and SLA language before we finalize.
